newsitem.title: SWEDEN: JULY NORSCAN PULP STOCKS UP 126,000 TONNES-SOURCE.
newsitem.headline: JULY NORSCAN PULP STOCKS UP 126,000 TONNES-SOURCE.

text.p: North American and Scandinavian (NorScan) pulp stocks, excluding Norway, rose 126,000 tonnes in July, an industry source said on Wednesday.
The rise brought NorScan stocks, excluding Norway, up to a total of 1.65 million tonnes in July, the source told Reuters.
"If we assume that Norwegian stocks rose by 3,000 tonnes in July to 45,000 tonnes, we land at an increase of 129,000 tonnes in July," the source said.
"If we include Norway, NorScan stocks amounted to about 1.7 million tonnes in July."
In Canada producer pulp stocks rose 39,000 in July to 771,000 tonnes, in the United States by 68,000 tonnes to 539,000, in Sweden by 11,000 tonnes to 259,000 and in Finland by 8,000 to 84,000.
"August is a question mark," the source said. "That month inventories are usually flat but September usually sees production halts, which may reduce stocks."

The rise in Canada occurred despite a forestry strike that started in mid-July. In British Columbia production the strike has stopped production at three companies, while production at another plant has stopped because of economic problems.
Earlier on Wednesday other company sources gave preliminary July figures, saying stocks rose by about 120,000 tonnes to just below 1.65 million tonnes in July from June.
